channel.title: Pharm Module 9 — Licit & illicit drugs, toxicology
channel.description: Her announcement: "Note key words and definitions eg addiction, dependence, as the L/O for this session will be tested in the Exam." Nobody lectured it, so this is her 41-slide deck as the answers you would write: the seven terms, stimulants and depressants, risk factors, interactions, where to refer, poisoning and antidotes, then her own four formative questions on it. Her rule for the deck holds: a slide with Pusheen the cat is the concept only, never its statistics or details. The questions are the tool's, in her format (a definition plus an example). The Pharm final: Thu 5 Nov, on campus · 80 min · 41 questions · 50 marks.

item.title: 01 · Start here: Module 9, and how she will test it
item.description: Her announcement: "Note key words and definitions eg addiction, dependence, as the L/O for this session will be tested in the Exam." Nobody lectured it, so this is her 41-slide deck as the answers you would write: the seven terms, stimulants and depressants, risk factors, interactions, where to refer, poisoning and antidotes, then her own four formative questions on it. Her rule for the deck holds: a slide with Pusheen the cat is the concept only, never its statistics or details. The questions are the tool's, in her format (a definition plus an example).

item.title: 02 · Licit and illicit drugs
item.description: Define a licit drug and an illicit drug, with an example of each.

item.title: 03 · Drug misuse and drug abuse
item.description: Define drug misuse and give an example. Define drug abuse and give an example. How is it different from misuse?

item.title: 04 · Drug dependence, and her correction
item.description: Define drug dependence. What is the difference between psychological and physical dependence? Give an example.

item.title: 05 · Drug addiction, and how it differs from dependence
item.description: Define drug addiction and give an example. How is addiction different from dependence?

item.title: 06 · Tolerance, withdrawal, and substance use disorder
item.description: Define drug tolerance and give an example. What is withdrawal? Give an example of its symptoms. What is a substance use disorder, and how is it diagnosed?

item.title: 07 · Stimulants and depressants
item.description: Is it a stimulant, a depressant, or both? (concept)

item.title: 08 · Who uses, and why: risk factors and drug use in Aotearoa
item.description: Name the four groups of risk factors for substance abuse in young adults, and give an example of one.

item.title: 09 · Interactions: the New Zealand Formulary and dangerous combinations
item.description: What is a medication-drug interaction, and how can a nurse check for one? Give an example.

item.title: 10 · The nurse's role, where to refer, and harm reduction
item.description: What is the nurse's role with a person whose substance use is a concern? Give an example of where a nurse can refer them. What is harm reduction? Give an example from Aotearoa New Zealand.

item.title: 11 · Poisoning, poisonous or venomous, and the Poisons Centre
item.description: Define poisoning. What is the difference between acute and chronic poisoning? Give an example. What is the difference between poisonous and venomous? Give an example of each. What is the National Poisons Centre, and when should someone call it?

item.title: 12 · Antidotes: naloxone and N-acetylcysteine
item.description: Define an antidote and give an example.

item.title: 13 · Her formative questions on Module 9
item.description: Her mini-exam 1, Q4: which description is accurate for dependence? Her test three, Q5: what is the definition of drug addiction? Her mini-exam 2, Q11: which statement is the most accurate about controlled drugs? Her mini-exam 3, Q4: after a half dose of an antibiotic by mistake, which step is NOT appropriate?
